publications.title: ESMA analysis shows continued growth in cross-border investment services
publications.summary: ESMA analysis shows continued growth in cross-border investment services 14 October 2026 Investor protection The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU’s financial markets regulator and supervisor, has completed its annual analysis of the cross-border provision of investment services , together with national competent authorities (NCAs). The exercise collected data from investment firms across 30 jurisdictions in the EU/EEA and found that cross-border investment activity continued to grow significantly in 2025. Key findings: A total of 379 financial firms provided cross-border services to retail clients. Approximately 15.5 million clients in the EU/EEA received investment services from firms located in other Member States, almost twice as many as in 2023 . publications.title: FINMA assesses the emergency and recovery plans for Zürcher Kantonalbank, Raiffeisen and PostFinance
publications.summary: The Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority FINMA has completed its annual assessment of the emergency and recovery plans for the domestic systemically important banks. The emergency plans for Zürcher Kantonalbank and Raiffeisen fulfil the regulatory requirements. The emergency plan for PostFinance does not yet meet all regulatory requirements. FINMA has once again approved the recovery plans for all three institutions.

publications.title: European Supervisory Authorities set priorities for 2027
publications.summary: European Supervisory Authorities set priorities for 2027 13 October 2026 Joint Committee The Joint Committee of the European Supervisory Authorities (EBA, EIOPA and ESMA – the ESAs) published today its Annual Work Programme for 2027 , setting out its priorities for addressing cross-sectoral risks and strengthening coordination across the European Union's financial sector. In 2027, the Joint Committee will focus on areas where cooperation among the three ESAs is essential to support financial stability, consumer protection and effective supervision. Key priorities include digital operational resilience, technological innovation, sustainable finance, securitisation and cross-sectoral risk monitoring.
